Inner Network Privacy Policy

Effective Date: October 10, 2026 · Last updated: October 10, 2026 · Version 2026-10-10

1. Who we are and what this Policy covers

Inner Network is operated by Wavecode, LLC, a Florida limited liability company ("Wavecode," "we," "us," or "our"). Our mailing address is 5937 NW 1st Ave, Miami, FL 33127, United States. You can reach us at contact@innernetwork.app.

This Privacy Policy explains what personal information we collect, why we collect it, how we use and share it, how long we keep it, and the choices and rights you have. It applies to:

  • the Inner Network mobile app for iPhone (and, when released, Android) (the "App");
  • our website at innernetwork.app, including the public business-card pages and event-preview pages that members can share by link (the "Website"); and
  • the emails and push notifications we send in connection with the App.

We refer to the App and Website together as the "Service." This Policy does not cover the practices of event organizers, news publishers, or other third-party websites that we link to. Those sites have their own policies.

Inner Network is a business and professional networking tool. It is not intended for personal, family, or household use, and it is not directed to children. See Section 14.

2. The short version

  • We collect the information you give us to build your professional profile, plus information about how you use the App.
  • We use your precise location only while the App is open, for two purposes: showing how far events are from you, and automatically confirming that you were at an event's venue if you said you were attending. We never store your raw GPS coordinates.
  • Your profile is visible to other signed-in members. You control which contact details appear on your card.
  • We do not sell your personal information, and we do not share it with advertisers or data brokers. We share it only with the service providers that run the App for us, with other members as described here, and when the law requires.
  • You can delete your account in the App at any time.
  • The App and Website do not use advertising cookies, tracking pixels, or third-party analytics.

The rest of this Policy gives the details.

3. Information we collect

3a. Information you give us

  • Account information. Your name, email address, and a password if you sign up with email. If you sign in with Apple, Google, or LinkedIn, we receive your name, email address, and (for Google and LinkedIn) your profile picture from that provider, and no password.
  • Profile ("digital business card") information. Job title, company, department, headline, short bio, years in the industry, professional role, industries, accreditations, interests, who you want to connect with, your card colors, and your profile photo. You may optionally add a phone number, office phone, company email, personal or company website, and LinkedIn or Instagram profile links.
  • Company email confirmation. If you add a company email whose domain matches your company website, we email a one-time link to that address so you can confirm you work there. We store the address, its domain, a one-time token, and the date it was confirmed.
  • Regions of activity. The Florida regions you tell us you work in. These are not shown on your card.
  • Connections, vouches, and passes. Who you ask to connect with, who you accept or decline, who you "pass" on, and endorsements ("vouches") you give to or receive from your connections.
  • Messages. Direct messages and group chats you send and receive in the App, including events you share into a chat.
  • Private contact notes, tags, and "where we met." Notes and tags you add about your own connections, and the event you choose as where you met them. Only you can see them.
  • Networking ROI records. If you use Networking ROI, the expenses you log (category, amount, date, an optional note, and the event or organization they belong to), the yearly membership dues you enter for an organization, and the people you record: either one of your connections or someone you type in by name, with their company, a note, how it went (met, follow-up, opportunity, or won), and an optional deal value. Only you can see them. We do not contact the people you record.
  • Expense receipts (not collected by us). Receipts you attach to an expense (photos or PDFs) are saved only on your phone and, if iCloud Drive is on, in your own iCloud Drive in an "Inner Network" folder. They are never uploaded to our servers, so we do not receive, read, or scan them. Apple stores your iCloud files under your Apple account. Deleting your Inner Network account does not delete files in your own iCloud Drive; you can remove them in the Files app.
  • Camera. The App uses your camera only when you ask it to: to scan another member's QR code (the image is read on your phone and is not uploaded or kept) or to photograph a receipt.
  • Lock screen QR code. If you tap "I'm here" at an event (or confirm attendance there), the App shows your business-card QR code, your name, and your next saved events on your lock screen until the event ends. Anyone who can see your lock screen can see those, and the QR code only opens the same public business card you already share. You can end it at any time.
  • Events you save, organizers you follow, and your RSVPs. Including whether you marked yourself as "going" to an event.
  • Reviews. Star ratings and written reviews of events and organizers, and whether you chose to post anonymously.
  • Events and organizers you create. If you add an event or organizer, we store what you enter, including any logo you upload.
  • Organizer claim requests. If you ask to claim an organizer listing, the contact email and comments you provide.
  • Reports and feedback. Reports you file about content or members, and feedback you send us.
  • Your acceptance of our Terms. The version of the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy you accepted and when.

3b. Information collected automatically when you use the App

  • Precise location (GPS). Only with your permission and only while the App is open. See Section 4 for exactly how this works.
  • Usage information. Which screens you open and which actions you take (for example, saving an event, sending a connection request, sharing an event, submitting a review). We record these against your account so we can understand which features are used. We do not use a third-party analytics service.
  • Session and presence information. When you open the App and when you were last active, so other members can see whether you are online (you can turn this off in Privacy settings) and so we can measure overall activity.
  • Push notification token. If you allow notifications, Apple (or Google, on Android) gives the App a device token, which we store so we can deliver notifications to your device.
  • Attendance confirmations. When the App automatically confirms you were at an event (Section 4), or when you answer the "Did you make it?" prompt, we record that confirmation.
  • Crash and diagnostic data. If the App crashes or hits an error, our crash-reporting provider (Sentry) receives technical details such as the device model, operating system version, App version, and what the App was doing at the time. We have configured it so it does not receive your name, email, user ID, IP address, screenshots, or the content of your screens.
  • Technical information. Like any internet service, our hosting providers (Supabase for the App's backend and GitHub Pages for the Website) receive your device's IP address and basic request information in their server logs. We do not use IP addresses to locate you or build a profile of you.

3c. Information we receive from others

  • Sign-in providers. Apple, Google, and LinkedIn send us your name, email address, and (Google and LinkedIn) profile picture when you choose to sign in or link your LinkedIn profile.
  • Other members. If another member connects with you, vouches for you, mentions you in a message, or adds a private note about you or records you in their Networking ROI, we receive that information.
  • Event organizers and public sources. Our event listings are gathered from organizers' public websites and event pages (see Section 8). Event pages may list speakers or hosts by name, title, and company. If you are listed as a speaker at an event we aggregate, we may hold your name, title, and company even if you are not an Inner Network member. Section 12 explains how to ask us to correct or remove this.

3d. Information we do not collect

We do not collect your contacts list, your calendar contents, your photos library (other than the single photo you pick as your profile picture or an organizer logo), payment card numbers, government identifiers, or advertising identifiers. We do not track you across other companies' apps or websites.

4. Precise location and attendance verification

This section is important, because precise location is treated as sensitive information under several U.S. state privacy laws. Here is exactly what we do.

When we ask. During onboarding, and again when you first use a distance-based filter, the App asks iOS for "While Using the App" location permission. We never ask for "Always" permission, and the App has no background location modes. If you say no, every other feature of the App keeps working.

What we use location for.

  1. Distance to events. To show how far an event is from you, to sort events by distance, and to filter the Discover and My Radar screens by distance. The App takes a single location reading when you open these screens; it does not track you continuously.
  2. Automatic attendance check-in. If you have marked yourself as "going" to an event, the event has a known venue location, and you open the App while the event is taking place, the App takes a single location reading. It sends your current latitude, longitude, and the reading's accuracy to our server together with the event ID. Our server calculates the distance between your reading and the venue. If you are within about 150 meters (roughly 500 feet), your attendance is marked "confirmed." If you are not, nothing is recorded.

What we store. We do not store your GPS coordinates. For a confirmed check-in, our server stores only: the fact that it was confirmed by GPS, the time, the calculated distance to the venue, the accuracy of the reading, the venue's own coordinates, and the 150-meter threshold that was applied. Your coordinates are used in that calculation and then discarded. When location is used for distance sorting, your coordinates are sent to our server to rank events and are not stored.

What "confirmed" means. A GPS confirmation means that a phone signed in to your account was near the venue during the event. It does not verify your identity, that you went inside, or that you participated. We describe it that way in the App.

Who can see it. By default, other members can see that you are "going" to an event and whether your attendance was confirmed. You can turn this off with the "Show My Event Attendance" and "Show Upcoming Events" switches in Account > Privacy. We also use attendance records, in aggregate and per member, to understand which events people actually attend.

How to turn it off. Go to iOS Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > Inner Network and choose "Never." You can also turn off Precise Location there. Without location, distance sorting and automatic check-in stop working and the rest of the App is unaffected. You can still confirm attendance manually when we ask "Did you make it?"

5. Push notifications and review prompts

With your permission we send push notifications for new messages (which include the sender's name and a short preview of the message), connection requests and acceptances, events shared with your team, job changes in your network, new events from organizers you follow, and occasional announcements from the Inner Network team sent as an in-app message. You can turn each category on or off in Account > Privacy & Notifications, or turn off all notifications in iOS Settings.

The App also schedules two local reminders on your device when you mark yourself as going to an event: one during the event ("Are you at …?") and one the next morning ("Did you make it to …?"). If you answer, we record your answer as a self-reported attendance confirmation, separate from GPS confirmation, and we invite you to leave a review. These reminders are created on your device and are cancelled if you sign out.

We do not send marketing text messages, and we do not currently send marketing emails. If we start a newsletter or other marketing email in the future, it will be opt-in, every message will include an unsubscribe link and our mailing address, and we will update this Policy first.

6. How we use your information

We use the information described above to:

  • create and maintain your account and digital business card;
  • show your card to other members and, when you choose to share it, to people you send your QR code or link to;
  • suggest members to connect with based on your role, industries, interests, regions, and who you want to meet;
  • deliver your messages and notifications;
  • show you events near you and confirm attendance as described in Section 4;
  • let you save events, follow organizers, review events and organizers, and vouch for connections;
  • let you track event expenses, membership dues, and the outcome of the people you meet (Networking ROI), and export your own report;
  • send transactional emails, such as email verification, password reset, company email confirmation, and notices about reports or moderation decisions affecting your account;
  • keep the Service secure, prevent abuse and spam, and enforce our Terms of Service;
  • understand how the App is used so we can fix problems and improve it;
  • respond to your support requests, reports, and feedback; and
  • comply with the law and protect our rights and the rights of our members.

We do not use your information for advertising, and we do not make decisions about you using automated profiling that has legal or similarly significant effects.

7. How we share your information

7a. With other members

Inner Network is a networking app, so sharing with other members is central to how it works. Every signed-in member can see your name, role, headline, bio, company, title, industries, interests, who you want to connect with, your vouches, and your LinkedIn and Instagram links if you added them. Your email, phone numbers, websites, and company email appear only if you turn the corresponding switch on when editing your card. Members can also see your upcoming events, the organizers you follow, your event attendance, and whether you are online, unless you turn those off in Account > Privacy. "Appear in People Search" and "Show My Card in Discovery" control whether members can find you through search and the connection deck.

Members you are connected to can download your card to their phone's Contacts and can export their connections (including the contact fields you have made visible) to a spreadsheet for their own use.

7b. With anyone who has a link you share

From Account you can generate a QR code and link to a read-only web version of your card, and any event can be shared as a link. Anyone who opens that link, including people who are not members, can see the card fields you have made visible plus your name, role, interests, and social links, or the event's details. These pages are marked so search engines should not index them, and the links are random and not listed anywhere; they only reach the people you or your contacts send them to. If you share your attendance to LinkedIn using the App's share feature, the image we generate includes your name, photo, and the event's organizer; nothing is posted unless you post it.

7c. With service providers that work for us

We use a small number of companies to run the Service. They receive only what they need to provide their service to us and are bound by their terms and data-processing agreements to use it only for that purpose.

7d. For legal reasons and safety

We may disclose information if we believe in good faith that it is required by law, subpoena, court order, or other legal process; to investigate or prevent fraud, abuse, or security issues; to enforce our Terms; or to protect the rights, property, or safety of Wavecode, our members, or the public.

7e. Business transfers

If Wavecode, LLC or the Inner Network business is involved in a merger, acquisition, financing, reorganization, bankruptcy, or sale of some or all of its assets, your information may be transferred to the acquiring or successor company as part of that transaction. If that happens, we will notify you through the App or by email before your information becomes subject to a different privacy policy, and the recipient will be required to honor the commitments in this Policy for information collected under it unless and until you are told otherwise and given a choice.

7f. With your direction

We share information when you ask us to, for example when you add an event to your Google or Outlook calendar (the event title, time, and location are passed to that calendar service) or open an organizer's website or a news article.

7g. We do not sell your personal information

We do not sell personal information, and we do not "share" it for cross-context behavioral advertising as those terms are defined in the California Consumer Privacy Act. We have not done so in the preceding 12 months. We do not knowingly sell or share the personal information of anyone under 16.

8. Event, organizer, and news information

Inner Network lists professional events gathered from organizers' public websites and event pages, and news headlines from industry publications. For events we store the event name, dates, venue, price, registration link, categories, a short excerpt (about 300 characters) of the organizer's description with a link to the organizer's page for the full text, and any speakers listed. For organizers we store the organization's name, website, event calendar link, a short description, and a logo where one has been provided. For news we store the headline, a short excerpt, the publisher's name, the link, and a link to the publisher's image.

This information is about organizations and public events, but it can include the names of individuals, such as speakers. We do not organize, sponsor, or endorse the events we list, and we are not affiliated with the organizers unless we say so. Organizers and individuals can ask us to correct or remove information about them; see our Content Removal and Correction Policy at innernetwork.app/takedown.html and Section 12.

9. Cookies and similar technologies

Website. innernetwork.app does not set cookies and does not use analytics tags, advertising pixels, or social media plug-ins. Our pages make requests to our own backend (Supabase) to load the shared card or event you asked for. The public card page loads three typefaces from Google Fonts, which means Google's servers receive the IP address of the visitor's browser; we plan to host these fonts ourselves. Because the Website uses no non-essential cookies or trackers, we do not show a cookie banner.

App. The App stores a small amount of information on your device so it works: your sign-in session in the iOS Keychain; a note that you accepted our Terms and completed onboarding; your chosen event filters; a cached copy of the event and organizer catalog so the App loads quickly and works offline; images for the home-screen widget (your name, title, and QR code) in a private container shared only with the widget; and rendered share images and spreadsheet exports you create. None of this is used for advertising or shared with anyone, and most of it is removed when you sign out or delete the App. The App does not use the Advertising Identifier (IDFA) and does not ask for App Tracking Transparency permission because it does not track you.

11. How we protect your information

We use the following measures. We describe them plainly because no system is perfectly secure and we do not want to overstate them.

  • All traffic between the App or Website and our servers uses HTTPS (TLS) encryption.
  • Our database enforces row-level security rules so that each request can only read or change the data that the signed-in member is allowed to see. Members cannot read each other's messages, private notes, or hidden contact fields.
  • Passwords are hashed by our authentication provider; we never see or store them in plain text. Sign in with Apple, Google, and LinkedIn means we never handle your password for those services.
  • Your sign-in session is stored in the iOS Keychain on your device.
  • Attendance verification happens on the server, and your GPS coordinates are not stored.
  • Crash reporting is configured not to collect personal information.
  • Administrative access to member data is limited to the owner of Wavecode, LLC and is logged.
  • Our hosting providers (Supabase on AWS, GitHub) maintain their own physical and network security programs.

If you believe your account has been compromised, email contact@innernetwork.app right away.

12. Your choices and rights

You can exercise most of these yourself in the App:

  • Access and correction. Account > Edit Profile shows and lets you change everything on your card. Your connections, saved events, followed organizers, and messages are visible in the App.
  • Visibility controls. When editing your card, tap the eye icon next to a field to show or hide it. In Account > Privacy you can turn off People Search, Discovery, event attendance, upcoming events, followed organizers, and online status.
  • Location and notifications. Control these in iOS Settings at any time. Nothing else in the App depends on them.
  • Blocking. You can block any member from their profile. Blocked members cannot message you or see you in the connection deck.
  • Deletion. Account > Delete Account permanently deletes your account and the information described in Section 10. You can also email us.
  • Portability. Email us and we will provide a copy of the personal information you have given us in a common, machine-readable format within 45 days.
  • Reviews. Email us to remove or anonymize a review you posted.
  • Non-members. If you are listed as a speaker, organizer contact, or otherwise appear in our event or organizer information and you want it corrected or removed, use the Report option on the event or organizer page or email us. See our Content Removal and Correction Policy.

To make a request by email, write to contact@innernetwork.app with the subject "Privacy request." We will need to verify that you are the account holder, usually by asking you to send the request from the email address on your account or to confirm a code we send to it. An authorized agent may submit a request on your behalf if they provide written permission from you and we can verify your identity. We respond within 45 days, and we may extend by another 45 days where permitted by law, in which case we will tell you. We will not treat you differently for exercising your rights. If we decline a request, we will tell you why, and you may appeal by replying to our decision; we will respond to an appeal within 45 days.

13. Information for residents of specific states

Several U.S. states have comprehensive privacy laws (including California, Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, Utah, Texas, Oregon, Montana, Iowa, Indiana, Tennessee, Delaware, New Jersey, New Hampshire, Kentucky, Nebraska, Maryland, Minnesota, and Rhode Island). Most of these laws apply only to businesses that exceed revenue or data-volume thresholds, and Inner Network is currently a small business that we believe falls below them. We nonetheless extend the rights in Section 12 to all of our users, wherever they live.

California. If you are a California resident, in the preceding 12 months we have collected the following categories of personal information as described in the California Consumer Privacy Act: identifiers (name, email, phone, account ID, device push token); professional or employment-related information (title, company, industry, accreditations); personal information described in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.80 (name, phone, email); internet or network activity (screens viewed, actions taken); precise geolocation (used only as described in Section 4 and not stored); audio, electronic, or visual information (your profile photo); inferences (member suggestions based on your stated role and interests); and sensitive personal information (precise geolocation, and your account log-in credentials). We use sensitive personal information only to provide the features you request and for security, and not to infer characteristics about you. The business purposes and recipients for each category are described in Sections 6 and 7. We do not sell or share personal information, so there is no "Do Not Sell or Share" setting to offer, and we do not use or disclose sensitive personal information for purposes that require a right to limit. You have the rights to know, delete, correct, and port your information and to be free from discrimination, as described in Section 12. California's "Shine the Light" law (Civil Code § 1798.83) lets you ask what personal information we have shared with third parties for their direct marketing; the answer is none.

Florida. The Florida Digital Bill of Rights (Fla. Stat. § 501.701 and following) imposes most of its obligations on "controllers" with more than $1 billion in global gross annual revenue that meet additional criteria. Wavecode, LLC does not meet those thresholds, so those provisions do not currently apply to us. Florida's Information Protection Act (Fla. Stat. § 501.171) does apply to us and governs how we protect and respond to breaches of personal information; see Section 15.

Nevada. We do not sell covered information as defined by Nevada law.

14. Children

The Service is for working professionals. You must be at least 18 years old to create an account, and signing up requires you to confirm this. We do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone under 18, and we do not direct the Service to children under 13 as defined by the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA). If you believe a child has created an account or that we hold a child's information, email contact@innernetwork.app and we will delete it promptly.

15. If there is a data breach

If we discover that personal information we hold has been accessed or acquired without authorization, we will investigate promptly, contain the problem, and, where the information could be used to harm you (for example, your email address together with your password or other credentials), notify affected individuals as quickly as we can and no later than 30 days after we determine a breach has occurred, as required by the Florida Information Protection Act (Fla. Stat. § 501.171), unless law enforcement asks us to delay. We will notify you by email at the address on your account, and by notice in the App or on the Website where appropriate. If a breach affects 500 or more Florida residents we will also notify the Florida Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days, and we will notify consumer reporting agencies and residents of other states as their laws require. We will also require our service providers to tell us about breaches affecting your information within 10 days of discovering them, as that Act requires.

16. Where your information is stored

Inner Network is offered to users in the United States, and our providers store information in the United States. If you use the Service from outside the United States, you understand that your information will be transferred to and processed in the United States. We do not currently target users in the European Union, the United Kingdom, or other regions with additional requirements; if we do in the future, we will update this Policy and our practices before doing so.

17. Changes to this Policy

When we change this Policy, we will update the Effective Date and version at the top. If the change is material, for example a new type of information collected, a new way we share it, or a new purpose, we will notify you in the App or by email before it takes effect and, where the change expands how we use information you already gave us, we will ask for your agreement. Earlier versions are available on request.
